Definition: from G4728; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly:--with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.
BiblicalUsage: We groan in this body, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven, and we groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body. Jesus Himself groans when He opens the ears of the deaf man: looking up to heaven, He sighed, and said, Ephphatha, Be opened.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the groaning is the sound of waiting for what God has promised, and even the Lord sighed before He healed.
